clue.text: A source of energy and relative growth

parts.note: a carb, short for carbohydrate, is a source of energy in the diet
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A dietitian lists an energy food and a family member's growing influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A source of energy' looks like the definition; it is the first piece, and the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a boil or abscess, a lump that grows on the skin.

clue.text: Island area or cape — climbing country

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, especially on the Thames
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A traveller lists an island, region or headland as places to scale in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a nation on the Adriatic coast of the Balkans.

clue.text: Eggs coming inside from hen

indicators.note: only the letters inside each word, without its ends, are taken from the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Eggs being brought indoors from the hen house.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs in a female fish.

clue.text: Anger after nude running showing a lack of necessary maturity

definitions.text: showing a lack of necessary maturity

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first in the answer
running suggests something loose and moving, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a fury after a streaker dashes past, behaving childishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' is the anagram signal on 'nude', and 'after' puts the anger word second.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone underage is too young for something legally, lacking the required years.

clue.text: Estuary language

definitions.meaning: The tongue of the Muscogee people of the south-eastern United States

explanation.surface: Estuary English, the accent of south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Estuary English, a London-area accent; both words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A creek is a narrow tidal inlet, and Creek is also a Native American tongue.

clue.text: European friend keeping very good herbal remedy

indicators.note: keeping means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A European friend swears by a highly effective herbal cure.
explanation.walkthrough: China = mate is cockney rhyming slang (china plate); the friend holds ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinacea, from the coneflower, is taken as a herbal medicine against colds.

clue.text: Most important horse is fed carefully at first

indicators.note: being fed means having something put into it, so the horse takes a letter inside

parts.note: a foal is a young horse

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A groom gently feeds a horse, taking care at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carefully' looks like an adverb on 'fed'; only its first letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The focal point is the central, chief one.

clue.text: Go very hungry dividing food around a million

indicators.note: the food goes around the following pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: fish is a food

explanation.surface: Sharing out a meal for a million leaves people starving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' and 'around' both say the food encloses 'a' and the million letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to starve, to suffer extreme hunger.

clue.text: Hot dish suggestion — learner's left to seek approval

parts.note: a curry is a spicy dish

indicators.note: left here means gone away, so the learner's letter departs from the word

parts.note: a flavour is a hint or suggestion
L is the learner plate, so learner's left is L has left

explanation.surface: A curry recipe tip: a learner cook has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learner's left' reads as 'learner has left': L comes out of FLAVOUR, giving FAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry favour is to try to win someone's approval by flattery.

clue.text: Freedom from parasites requiring careful attention getting rid of one

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects

indicators.note: getting rid of means the letter for one is thrown out of the word

parts.note: nice in its old sense means delicate or needing precision, as in a nice distinction
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Ridding a child of nits needs painstaking attention.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE in its sense 'fine, subtle' loses I, leaving NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence means freedom to act as one pleases, as in poetic licence.

clue.text: More than a couple of Italians running late

parts.note: over means more than
due is Italian for two, a couple to Italians

explanation.surface: More than two Italians are behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, past the time expected.

clue.text: Address mostly full of comic potential in epic style

parts.note: one's home is one's address

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: rich can mean highly amusing, as in 'that's rich'

explanation.surface: A speech largely packed with humour, delivered in grand manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a speech; it is a place you live. RICH loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means in the grand manner of Homer's epics, the Iliad and Odyssey.

clue.text: Keep time or we go wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means getting mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Stick to schedule, or things will fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep time' reads as a phrase; 'Keep' is a castle's stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: The keep is the main tower of a castle.

clue.text: With good intentions, PM's lacking style going round poor

indicators.note: going round means the outer letters encircle the next piece
lacking means a piece is missing from the word

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington was a British Prime Minister; the 's is 'is'
ton is fashion or style
mean can mean poor or shabby

explanation.surface: A prime minister without flair, well-intentioned, tours the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The PM is the Duke of Wellington; 'lacking' drops the style word, and 'going round' wraps the rest round the poor word.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-meaning describes someone whose aims are kind, even if results fall short.

clue.text: Novelist, not English, has new name for town

indicators.note: not means the letter for English is left out

parts.note: Charles Kingsley wrote The Water-Babies and Westward Ho!

explanation.surface: A writer, not English, adopts a fresh name for a place.
explanation.definitionFit: King's Lynn is a market town and port in Norfolk, eastern England.

clue.text: Real logic dealt badly with hidden meaning

indicators.note: something dealt badly is mishandled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sound reasoning poorly handled in a story with a secret message.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegoric work carries a symbolic sense beneath its literal story.

clue.text: Finding new home for unfortunate neighbours losing billions

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone awry, so the remaining letters are rearranged
losing means a letter is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Councils rehome hapless neighbours after they lose a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: NEIGHBOURS less B gives NEIGHOURS, which 'unfortunate' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehousing is providing people with different accommodation.

clue.text: Nielsen, perhaps omitting start of chorus from ballet

indicators.note: omitting means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: ballet is a form of dance

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of chorus

explanation.surface: A dancer named Nielsen skips the opening chorus of a ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Nielsen as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer, so he is an example of a person from Denmark.

clue.text: Exploit computer key to copy both sides of advert

parts.note: Esc is the escape key

indicators.note: the copying word sits on both sides of the advert, enclosing it

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Instructions to press a key and duplicate an advert's edges for gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides of advert' looks like taking the outer letters of 'advert'; instead the copy word sits on both sides of the short advert.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is an adventurous exploit or prank.

clue.text: Card from company doctor

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A greetings card from the firm's medical officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To card wool is to comb out its fibres.

clue.text: What's outstanding in New England? Better eastern seafood

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
cod is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A diner asks what's best in New England: better East Coast fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' is literal: a cape projects out from the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is a peninsula jutting into the Atlantic from Massachusetts, a cape standing out from the land.

clue.text: Memorial for Bradley?

definitions.meaning: a grave marker commemorating the dead
Bradley ... is the schoolmaster in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend; the query marks it as a name

explanation.surface: A monument for someone called Bradley.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is a gravestone, and Bradley Headstone is a Dickens character.

clue.text: Very active Conservative splitting left

indicators.note: splitting means the letter sits inside the word, dividing it

parts.note: exited means left, went out

explanation.surface: A Tory dividing the left wing gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks political; it means went out.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited means stirred up, highly energised.

clue.text: Songbird left where it could be trapped?

parts.note: a bird could be caught in a net

explanation.surface: A songbird is left where a bird-catcher might snare it.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch known for its song.

clue.text: Statement offering little put detail awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily arranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A remark that adds little, with its specifics clumsily presented.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark with little meaning.

clue.text: Record single rising — around number four in chart

indicators.note: around means the reversed word encloses the next letter
in a down entry rising means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: lone means single

indicators.note: number four in means the fourth letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A single climbs to near number four in the hit parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LONE into ENOL, which goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to record one's name on a list or register.

clue.text: Gold jaguars Inca regularly displayed

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Golden jaguar figures were often on show among the Inca.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric means of or containing gold, from Latin aurum.

clue.text: Reduced voucher against wine

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the voucher word loses its final letter

parts.note: a chit is a note or voucher
anti means against

explanation.surface: A discount coupon is set against a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced voucher' sounds like a discount; it is CHIT shortened to CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red Italian wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Test chemical engineers by proxy

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
an agent acts as a proxy

explanation.surface: Engineers test a chemical through a stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used in a chemical reaction to detect another.

clue.text: Mistake taking rook with queen

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess blunder: capturing a rook with the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make an error, to go wrong.

clue.text: A number really get Information Technology

parts.note: to dig is slang for really understanding or liking

explanation.surface: Quite a few people truly understand computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any of the numerals from zero to nine.

clue.text: Note former cane plant with yellow flowers

parts.note: G is a musical note
olden means of former times
a rod is a cane

explanation.surface: A record of an old cane plant with yellow blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a perennial of the genus Solidago with sprays of yellow flowers.
